## 7. Compiler support and behavior {#compiler}

**Use the exact target and inspect the emitted sequence.** The full analysis is now in [LLVM on RDNA: WMMA dependencies and waits](../rdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd).

### Target support and tools {#compiler-target-lookup}

Scope: `gfx1100–gfx1103`, `gfx1150–gfx1153`, and `gfx1200/1201`. Native availability remains beside the [SWMMAC](#matrix-operands-row-5), [FP8 conversion](#fp8-availability-row-1), and [packed atomic](#packed-atomic-availability-row-1) comparisons. [Compiler targets and ISA tools](../rdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#compiler-target-lookup) gives the supporting interfaces.

### Compiler takeaways {#compiler-summary}

- **D → A/B overlap:** LLVM inserts one vector no-op for a recognized, unseparated dependency; GFX12 also checks the sparse index. [Exact detection and separator](../rdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#llvm-wmma-spacing).
- **D → C only:** that WMMA fix does not add a vector no-op. ISA stall conditions still apply. [C-only conditions](../rdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#llvm-wmma-c-only).
- **Memory readiness and optional ALU delay:** separate mechanisms with their own eligibility and limits. [Memory waits](../rdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#memory-waits) · [Optional controls and inline assembly](../rdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#developer-boundaries).

### Applicability and validation limits {#native-availability}

The analysis is pinned to LLVM `4e9d349ab86d` and recognized machine instructions in the reviewed pipelines. Source and regression expectations were inspected; LLVM regression tests and GPU execution were not performed. [Full revision, coverage and limits](../rdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#compiler-evidence).
